source: Consistent with this model, loss of minar2 markedly reduces cholesterol distribution in the hair bundles, causes longer and thinner hair bundles, and gives rise to enlarged and aggregated apical lysosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by Lamp1-GFP labeling shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: Defects in minar2 mutant likely compromise mechanotransduction, reduce the number of hair cells, and result in hearing loss.
source: These defects in minar2 mutant likely compromise mechanotransduction, reduce the number of hair cells, and result in hearing loss.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined phenotypic data including AM1-43 labeling, hair cell counts, and hearing tests.

claim: The effects of minar2 loss-of-function are mimicked by drug treatment that reduces the cholesterol levels in the hair bundles.
source: Our model is further supported by results from pharmacological interventions. The effects of minar2 loss-of-function are mimicked by drug treatment that reduces the cholesterol levels in the hair bundles, while these effects are reversed by treatment that increases the cholesterol levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by 2HPβCD and U18666A treatment data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The effects of minar2 loss-of-function are reversed by treatment that increases the cholesterol levels.
source: Our model is further supported by results from pharmacological interventions. The effects of minar2 loss-of-function are mimicked by drug treatment that reduces the cholesterol levels in the hair bundles, while these effects are reversed by treatment that increases the cholesterol levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by efavirenz and voriconazole treatment data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is a previously understudied gene and is present in vertebrate species only.
source: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is a previously understudied gene and is present in vertebrate species only.
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 knockout causes profound deafness in mice.
source: Previous mouse genetic screening for hearing loss genes showed that Kiaa1024L/Minar2 knockout causes profound deafness (Bowl et al., 2017; Ingham et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bowl et al., 2017 and Ingham et al., 2019.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is essential for normal hearing in vertebrates.
source: Our study presented here, together with the results in the mouse model, highlights that Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is essential for normal hearing in vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results in zebrafish and mice.

claim: Hearing defects in minar2 mutants exist at the level of hair cells.
source: Our results with mutant zebrafish reveal that hearing defects exist at the level of hair cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the hair cell-specific phenotypes observed in the mutants.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is highly enriched in hair cells in the vertebrate inner ears.
source: This conclusion is consistent with the highly enriched expression of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 in the hair cells in the vertebrate inner ears, as shown by our in situ hybridization results and our surveys of FACS and single-cell RNA sequencing data (Barta et al., 2018; Elkon et al., 2015; Erickson and Nicolson, 2015; Liu et al., 2018; Steinhart et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization and sequencing data analysis.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is expressed in various regions in the brain tissue.
source: Outside the inner ear, Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is also expressed in various regions in the brain tissue, and a previous study showed that loss of Minar2 in mice impairs motor function and reduces the number of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons (Ho et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is stated based on known expression patterns.

claim: Loss of Minar2 in mice impairs motor function and reduces the number of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons.
source: Outside the inner ear, Kiaa1024L/Minar2 is also expressed in various regions in the brain tissue, and a previous study showed that loss of Minar2 in mice impairs motor function and reduces the number of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons (Ho et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ho et al., 2020.

claim: The degree of hearing loss in mutant minar2fs139 zebrafish larvae is not as severe as it was in the adult knockout mouse.
source: The degree of hearing loss in mutant minar2fs139 zebrafish larvae is not as severe as it was in the adult knockout mouse.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of phenotypes between zebrafish and mouse models.

claim: Minar2 knockout mice have degeneration of hair cells and progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
source: A recently published study showed that Minar2 knockout mice had degeneration of hair cells and progressive sensorineural hearing loss (Bademci et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bademci et al., 2022.

claim: The reduction of inner ear hair cell numbers in mutant minar2fs139 zebrafish is progressive, worsening from no changes in the larval stage to a 30% reduction in the adult stage.
source: In mutant minar2fs139 zebrafish, the reduction of inner ear hair cell numbers is progressive, worsening from no changes in the larval stage to a 30% reduction in the adult stage.
evidence: This claim is supported by hair cell counting data at different developmental stages shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and Figure 1F.

claim: In zebrafish, hair cells are continuously generated until late in adulthood.
source: We note that unlike the mouse model, in which the hair cells are generated in early development and cannot regenerate in the adult stage (Atkinson et al., 2015; Basch et al., 2016; Driver and Kelley, 2020), in zebrafish the hair cells are continuously generated until late in adulthood (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on hair cell regeneration.

claim: In the mouse model, hair cells are generated in early development and cannot regenerate in the adult stage.
source: We note that unlike the mouse model, in which the hair cells are generated in early development and cannot regenerate in the adult stage (Atkinson et al., 2015; Basch et al., 2016; Driver and Kelley, 2020), in zebrafish the hair cells are continuously generated until late in adulthood (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on hair cell development.

claim: Defects in mechanotransduction, longer and thinner hair bundles, and enlarged apical lysosomes observed in kiaa1024L/minar2 mutant indicate that Kiaa1024L/Minar2 acts primarily in the apical region and the hair bundle in hair cells.
source: Defects in mechanotransduction, longer and thinner hair bundles, and enlarged apical lysosomes observed in kiaa1024L/minar2 mutant all indicate that Kiaa1024L/Minar2 acts primarily in the apical region and the hair bundle in hair cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined phenotypic observations.

claim: GFP or FLAG-tagged Minar2 protein is primarily localized to the apical endo-membranes and stereocilia membranes.
source: GFP or FLAG-tagged Minar2 protein is primarily localized to the apical endo-membranes and stereocilia membranes, which are the appropriate locations to exert the above functions.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The apical region of the hair cell is crowded with endocytotic vesicles, including abundant lysosomes.
source: Previous studies showed that the apical region of the hair cell is crowded with endocytotic vesicles, including abundant lysosomes (Krey et al., 2018; Revelo et al., 2014; Spicer et al., 1999; Wiwatpanit et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Endocytotic membrane-bound structures are thought to transport ions and other materials to and fro towards the apical entry of the hair cells.
source: These endocytotic membrane-bound structures are thought to transport ions and other materials to and fro towards the apical entry of the hair cells (Spicer et al., 1999), but the functions of these structures are not well characterized.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Spicer et al., 1999.

claim: Loss of lysosomal mucolipins in cochlear hair cells gives rise to abnormally enlarged lysosomes at the apical region.
source: One recent study showed that loss of lysosomal mucolipins in cochlear hair cells gives rise to abnormally enlarged lysosomes at the apical region. These aberrant lysosomes are toxic to cells and cause hair cell loss (Wiwatpanit et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wiwatpanit et al., 2018.

claim: Aberrant lysosomes are toxic to cells and cause hair cell loss.
source: One recent study showed that loss of lysosomal mucolipins in cochlear hair cells gives rise to abnormally enlarged lysosomes at the apical region. These aberrant lysosomes are toxic to cells and cause hair cell loss (Wiwatpanit et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wiwatpanit et al., 2018.

claim: The stereocilia membrane is densely covered with filipin-induced deformation in freeze-fracture preparation of hair cells.
source: Previous studies showed that the stereocilia membrane is densely covered with filipin-induced deformation in the freeze-fracture preparation of hair cells, indicating the presence of abundant cholesterol in the stereocilia membrane (Forge et al., 1988; Forge and Richardson, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Forge et al., 1988 and Forge and Richardson, 1993.

claim: Cholesterol may stiffen biological membranes.
source: Previous studies showed that cholesterol may stiffen biological membranes (Chakraborty et al., 2020; Dimova, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on cholesterol's effects on membrane mechanics.

claim: When cholesterol is depleted from hair cell membranes following methyl β cyclodextrin treatment, an apparent loss of structural integrity and 'floppy' hair bundles are observed.
source: When cholesterol was depleted from hair cell membranes following methyl β cyclodextrin treatment, an apparent loss of structural integrity and 'floppy' hair bundles were observed (Purcell et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Purcell et al., 2011.

claim: The stereocilia tip membranes can serve as a component of the gating spring of the MET channel.
source: It has been suggested that the stereocilia tip membranes can serve as a component of the gating spring of the MET channel (Powers et al., 2014; Powers et al., 2012), although this has currently been debated (Bartsch et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Powers et al., 2014 and Powers et al., 2012, but noted as debated.

claim: The mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 interacts with cholesterol and this interaction is essential for the spatiotemporal activity of Piezo1.
source: Previous studies showed that the mechanosensitive ion channel Piezo1 interacts with cholesterol and this interaction is essential for the spatiotemporal activity of Piezo1 (Buyan et al., 2020; Ridone et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Buyan et al., 2020 and Ridone et al., 2020.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 may be responsible for or facilitate the apical transport of cholesterol to the hair bundles.
source: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 may be responsible for or facilitate the apical transport of cholesterol to the hair bundles.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the localization and function of Minar2.

claim: The subcellular localization of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 in both the apical endo-membranes and the hair bundle membranes is consistent with a transporting role for Kiaa1024L/Minar2.
source: The subcellular localization of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 in both the apical endo-membranes and the hair bundle membranes is consistent with a transporting role for Kiaa1024L/Minar2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the localization data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The apical transport defects caused by the loss of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 can explain the marked decrease of accessible cholesterol levels in the hair bundles.
source: The apical transport defects caused by the loss of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 can explain the marked decrease of accessible cholesterol levels in the hair bundles.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of cholesterol distribution changes in the mutant.

claim: The decrease of accessible cholesterol is expected to bring about the up-regulation of genes downstream of Srebp2.
source: Because the accessible cholesterol is the critical determinant for cholesterol homeostasis regulation (Lange and Steck, 2016; Lange et al., 2004), the decrease of accessible cholesterol is expected to bring about the up-regulation of genes downstream of Srebp2, which is indeed observed in the minar2 mutant.
evidence: This claim is inferred from known cholesterol homeostasis mechanisms and supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The observed enlarged aggregated lysosome and decreased number of hair cells are likely a result of the transportation defects.
source: According to this model, the observed enlarged aggregated lysosome and decreased number of hair cells are likely a result of the transportation defects.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the proposed model.

claim: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein belongs to a protein family that also includes the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
source: Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein belongs to a protein family that also includes the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
evidence: This claim is based on protein family classification.

claim: This protein family is defined by a conserved but uncharacterized protein family domain (UPF0258) located at the carboxy ends of the proteins.
source: This protein family is defined by a conserved but uncharacterized protein family domain (UPF0258) located at the carboxy ends of the proteins.
evidence: This claim is based on protein domain analysis.

claim: Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor acts as a negative regulator of mTOR signaling through its interaction with the Deptor protein.
source: Our previous study showed that Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor acts as a negative regulator of mTOR signaling through its interaction with the Deptor protein, an integral component of the mTORC complex (Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2018.

claim: Loss of the ubtor gene in zebrafish causes motor hyperactivity and epilepsy-like behaviors by elevating neuronal activity and activating mTOR signaling.
source: Loss of the ubtor gene in zebrafish causes motor hyperactivity and epilepsy-like behaviors by elevating neuronal activity and activating mTOR signaling (Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2021.

claim: Ubtor/MINAR1 plays a role in angiogenesis and breast cancer.
source: It has also been shown that Ubtor/MINAR1 plays a role in angiogenesis and breast cancer (Ho et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ho et al., 2018.

claim: The region in Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor that interacts with the Deptor protein is missing in the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein.
source: Since the region in Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor that interacts with the Deptor protein is missing in the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein, the regulation of mTOR signaling is likely a function specific to the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
evidence: This claim is based on protein sequence comparison.

claim: The regulation of mTOR signaling is likely a function specific to the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
source: Since the region in Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor that interacts with the Deptor protein is missing in the Kiaa1024L/Minar2 protein, the regulation of mTOR signaling is likely a function specific to the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the absence of the Deptor-binding region in Minar2.

claim: The cholesterol-binding region identified in this study is conserved in the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein.
source: Because the cholesterol-binding region that we identify in this study is conserved in the Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor protein, it should be interesting to investigate whether Kiaa1024/Minar1/Ubtor also plays a role in the regulation of cholesterol.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: The human ortholog MINAR2 is specifically expressed by the auditory hair cells.
source: Because of the conserved requirement of Kiaa1024L/Minar2 gene orthologs for hearing in both mice and zebrafish, and that the human ortholog MINAR2 is also specifically expressed by the auditory hair cells (Steinhart et al., 2022), it will be important to examine whether KIAA1024L/MINAR2 gene mutations may underline hearing abnormalities in humans.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Steinhart et al., 2022.

claim: Mutations in MINAR2 cause deafness in human patients.
source: Indeed, while this study was under review, it was reported that mutations in MINAR2 cause deafness in human patients (Bademci et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bademci et al., 2022.
